title: ELIZA Publication
summary: Joseph Weizenbaum's paper describing ELIZA was published in the January 1966 issue of Communications of the ACM. The paper describes ELIZA as a program operating within MIT's MAC time-sharing system that enables certain kinds of natural-language conversation between a person and a computer, using keyword-triggered decomposition rules and associated reassembly rules.
significance: A primary-source publication milestone for the documented ELIZA conversational program, recorded without inferring a separate creation or release date.

verification.note: The ACM Digital Library records the ELIZA paper in Communications of the ACM, Volume 9, Issue 1, January 1966, pages 36-45, DOI 10.1145/365153.365168. This candidate records the publication milestone only. It does not infer ELIZA's exact creation date, public release date, development geography beyond what the paper itself states about operation within MIT's MAC time-sharing system, ancestry, influence, causality, or relationship edges.
